test_title: PYST 35: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A thief takes off on his bike at a certain speed, after seeing a police car at a distance of 250 m. The police car starts chasing the thief and catches him. If the thief runs 1.5 km before being caught and the speed of the police car is 70 km/h, then what is the speed of thief's bike (in km/h)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time of travel is constant, the ratio of speeds is directly proportional to the ratio of distances covered.

Ratio of distances = Distance of Police : Distance of Thief = (1.5 + 0.25) : 1.5 = 1.75 : 1.50 = 7 : 6

⇒ Speed of Police : Speed of Thief = 7 : 6

Given 7 units = 70 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed of Thief = 6 units = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between the police car and the thief = 250 m = 0.25 km

Distance run by the thief before being caught = 1.5 km

Speed of the police car = 70 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/622705a71e94e381158a4c1af694953d0c7835029131c7fbc5b41a313a3bb646.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance covered by the police car = 1.5 km + 0.25 km = 1.75 km

⇒ Total distance covered by the thief = 1.5 km

⇒ Time taken by both the police car and the thief to reach the catch point is equal.

⇒ Distance of Police ÷ Speed of Police = Distance of Thief ÷ Speed of Thief

⇒ 1.75 ÷ 70 = 1.5 ÷ Speed of Thief

⇒ Speed of Thief = (1.5 × 70) ÷ 1.75

⇒ Speed of Thief = 105 ÷ 1.75 = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Constant Time Concept

If two bodies travel for the exact same duration of time, the ratio of the distances they cover is directly proportional to the ratio of their speeds (D₁ / D₂ = S₁ / S₂).
